text: In 107 operable non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients, immunohistochemical PD-ECGF/TP (thymidine phosphorylase) expression was high in 25% and associated with high vascular grade (P=0.01; 44% of high-grade vs 17% of low/medium). It was more frequent in T2 than T1 tumours (P=0.04). Overall survival was unaffected (P=0.09), but node-negative patients with positive expression had worse prognosis (P=0.04), indicating a more aggressive phenotype. Separately, a retrospective study of 275 breast cancer patients found elevated platelet distribution width-to-platelet count ratio (PDW/P) correlated with age and HER2 status. Univariate analysis linked PDW, MPV, PDW/P, tumour size, nuclear grade and lymph node involvement to inferior disease-free survival; multivariate analysis identified large tumour size (HR 3.24, 95% CI 1.24–8.47) and elevated PDW/P (HR 2.99, 95% CI 1.18–7.57) as independent prognostic factors (p<0.05).
